You shouldn't brush your teeth after exposing them to acids. You need to wait awhile before brushing because the acid softens the enamel. It will eventually harden back up but if you brush while it's soft you are literally brushing it off your teeth.
I use powdered lime juice myself, but yeah, it's good stuff.

Don't overdo it. You can add a little to make some savory dishes a bit sour, and you can add a little to some sweet stuff to make it a bit tart, but acids in cooking should be used sparingly. This is why, for example, you add a few capfulls of red wine vinegar to tomato sauce to make it awesome. In pickling however, you use a lot (1/8 volume) to get the job done (you have to add 1/16 volume of salt to kill most bacteria for a few days - allowing the bacteria that can survive in a saline solution to break down the food, and then after 3 days you add an acid to STOP the fermentation). That's a different story altogether though.
